newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aborigines at risk of major HIV epidemic - report.
newsitem.headline: Aborigines at risk of major HIV epidemic - report.

text.p: A major HIV epidemic threatens to break out among Australia's Aborigines who have been left behind in the nation's decade-old fight against the AIDS virus, an official report said on Wednesday.

Stung by the report's findings, the government immediately said it would spend A$12 million (US$9.4 million) over two years to curb the growing incidence of the human immuno-deficiency virus (HIV) among indigenous people.

"It is sobering to reflect on the fact that it is 15 years into the epidemic and only now are we truly addressing the special needs of Aborigines and Torres Strait islanders in a comprehensive and integrated way," Health Minister Michael Wooldridge said in a statement.
He was responding to a report by an AIDS advisory body which found rates of HIV infection among indigenous people were rising while rates for the rest of the population were falling.
HIV can lead to acquired immune deficiency syndrome or AIDS, a deadly, incurable condition which can be sexually transmitted.
The report warned of a major epidemic among mainland Aborigines and communities living on the Torres Strait islands between Australia's northern tip and Papua New Guinea.
It blamed poor basic health services and a relatively high rate of sexually transmitted diseases in Aboriginal communities.

Information on HIV infection rates among Aborigines is patchy, the report said. Available statistics show HIV infection rates among Aborigines are to similar to those among non-indigenous people, but Aboriginal rates are now rising.
"These data all support the conclusion that a major outbreak of HIV infection among Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities is probable," the report said.
So far, 128 cases of HIV have been reported for indigenous people, including 34 deaths from AIDS, the report said. Aborigines make up 300,000 of the nation's 18 million people.
About 480 new cases of HIV are reported in Australia each year. About 15,600 Australians were estimated by health authorities to have contracted HIV as of June 1996.
